It gets in touch with an agency that has a network of clients with high income customers (such as high-end supermarkets) and asks the agency to create profiles of young parents or couples who can be assumed to be wealthy and to have a new child, so that these can later be used to present advertising within partner apps based on those profiles."],"name":"Create profiles for personalised advertising","description":"Information about your activity on this service (such as forms you submit, content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (for example, information from your previous activity on this service and other websites or apps) or similar users. Global assets have once more felt the aftershocks of Trump’s tariffs decisions after the US president announced a 15 per cent blanket tariff following the Supreme Court’s rebuke.

 

Bitcoin fell sharply amid the uncertainty, falling as much as 4.8 per cent to $64,300 (£47,531), sparked by investors pulling away from speculative assets and concerns about future cryptocurrency regulation.

 

The currency has lost nearly half its value since October, where it hit a record high of $126,210.50. Digital token Ether, also tumbled 5.2 per cent.

 

Meanwhile, gold prices rallied to their highest level in more than three weeks, as tariff uncertainty weighed down the dollar and drove investors to the safe haven asset.

 

The asset inched up 0.7 per cent to $51,45.99 per ounce, while silver jumped 2.8 per cent to $87.24.

    By Maisie Grice

    Bitcoin sinks while golds shine amid Trump turmoil

    Global assets have once more felt the aftershocks of Trump’s tariffs decisions after the US president announced a 15 per cent blanket tariff following the Supreme Court’s rebuke.

     

    Bitcoin fell sharply amid the uncertainty, falling as much as 4.8 per cent to $64,300 (£47,531), sparked by investors pulling away from speculative assets and concerns about future cryptocurrency regulation.

     

    The currency has lost nearly half its value since October, where it hit a record high of $126,210.50. Digital token Ether, also tumbled 5.2 per cent.

     

    Meanwhile, gold prices rallied to their highest level in more than three weeks, as tariff uncertainty weighed down the dollar and drove investors to the safe haven asset.

     

    The asset inched up 0.7 per cent to $51,45.99 per ounce, while silver jumped 2.8 per cent to $87.24.

    It’s looking like a dip on open for the FTSE 100 this morning – albeit a modest one.

     

    That’s according to futures data from IG, which says London’s blue-chip index is in for a 0.2 per cent slump following Trump raising tariffs on the UK by five per cent after his 15 per cent baseline tariff was applied across trading partners.

     

    Now the move is hardly a brash reaction for the FTSE 100, which has been on a blistering run as of late, sealing multiple record closes last week.

     

    Elsewhere, the pound is showing some strength against the dollar at $1.35.

     

    Sterling took a tumble last week but clawed back some gains after Friday’s Supreme Court tariff ruling and has continued to build on those this morning, taking five day performance to a 0.3 per cent gain.
